summary: Priest Lake lookout site: the 1929 cupola cabin still stands, the 1939 L-4 pole tower and the 1977 steel tower are gone, and restoration was planned for 2026.

facts.status_note: The 1929 cupola cabin still stands. The 1939 pole tower fell in the 1960s, and the 1977 steel tower and wooden cab were removed in 2017 or 2019.

access.note: Hike-in and abandoned. The sources do not give current entry rules. A 2006 visit report notes a large hole in the floor by the door.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in. Idaho Fire Lookouts warns the last 6 miles of road to the trailhead are rough. Ask the Idaho Department of Lands about access before going.

events.note: First used for fire detection as a patrol point.
Cupola cabin, called L-2 by firelookout.com. The register says the cupola structure was completed in 1929.
50-foot pole tower with L-4 cab. The register calls it CCC-built.
Abandoned as an active fire detection site.
Pole tower collapsed around 1965 per the register. firelookout.com says it fell in the 1960s.
Steel tower moved from Packsaddle Lookout and topped with a wooden cab by the Idaho Department of Lands. The register gives a 12 x 12 cab; firelookout.com gives 15 x 15.
Cupola cabin restored. The register gives 1983-1992; Idaho Fire Lookouts says the 1980s.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, December 20, 1993.
Vandals damaged the tower and the wooden cab was removed, per firelookout.com.
Idaho Fire Lookouts says the 1977 steel tower was dismantled.
Restoration and rebuilding planned, with completion estimated for 2026, per Idaho Fire Lookouts.

corrections.why: The standing structure is the 1929 cupola cabin, which firelookout.com calls L-2. The L-4 cab belonged to a 1939 pole tower that fell in the 1960s.
15.2 m (50 ft) matches the 1939 pole tower, which is gone. The sources give no current tower height.
The register's listing describes the cupola cabin. The tower it once carried was removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say Idaho Department of Lands. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives Kaniksu National Forest. The story uses the Idaho Department of Lands.
The register gives a 12 x 12 wooden cab. firelookout.com gives 15x15. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives a 25-foot steel base and 15x15 cabin, while firelookout.com says 20 feet.
firelookout.com says the wooden cab was removed after vandal damage in 2017. Idaho Fire Lookouts says the steel tower was dismantled in 2019 and that an L-4 cab is set to be replaced in 2025/26.

notes_for_editor: Current status is unclear. Idaho Fire Lookouts says a restoration was planned for 2026 and an L-4 cab is set for replacement in 2025/26, which conflicts with its own 2019 dismantling entry. The SAH Archipedia and Library of Congress pages returned 403 and were not used. SummitPost is out of date (says a 1977 tower is still used). The register's visit report dates to 2006. The record's L-4 design and 15.2 m height describe the 1939 pole tower, not the standing cupola.
